item.title: Clark yells in referee's face as decisions go against her side
item.description:
Frustration Boils Over: Clark’s Confrontation with Referee Highlights Growing Tensions in the WNBA

Caitlin Clark’s face turned beet red as she stood toe to toe with referee Gerda Gatling on the Gainbridge Fieldhouse floor in Indianapolis. The Indiana Fever guard, a three-time All-Star and one of the biggest names in women’s basketball, was seething with anger after a night of contentious calls went against her team in an 88-75 defeat at the hands of the Golden State Valkyries. Clark’s ire was directed squarely at Gatling, and in a moment that will be replayed for weeks to come, she let her frustrations boil over into a heated exchange with the official.

item.title: World Cup 2026: Tuchel takes blame amid speculation over England future; Argentina players criticised for banner – live
item.description:
England’s World Cup Exit: A Tale of Misplaced Confidence and Unfathomable Tactics

The streets of Buenos Aires are alive with the sound of celebrating Argentines, their sky blue and white jerseys a sea of color as they dance in the streets and wave flags from balconies high above the traffic. It’s a scene that’s been played out in many a World Cup city before, but for England fans, the bitter taste of defeat is still fresh in their mouths. As the team’s coach, Thomas Tuchel, takes the blame for England’s exit from the World Cup, questions are being asked about the tactics that led to this outcome.

item.title: Wales pick Lake against Boks after injury scare
item.description:
Injury Scare Behind Lake’s Selection

Wales’ touring captain Dewi Lake has been named in the starting side for the Nations Championship match against South Africa in Durban on Saturday, despite being a major doubt for the clash due to a recent injury scare. The hooker hobbled off in last weekend’s defeat by Argentina, sparking concerns that he may not be fit to face the world champions.

However, head coach Steve Tandy has opted to stick with Lake, who has been selected alongside a new-look centre combination featuring Ben Thomas and Max Llewellyn. The duo will form a crucial partnership in the midfield, as Wales look to test themselves against the physical might of the Springboks.

item.title: Tuchel vows to remain as England head coach after Argentina defeat
item.description:
England’s Semi-Final Bittersweet: Tuchel Vows to See Through Euro 2028 Commitment

In the aftermath of a World Cup semi-final defeat at the hands of Argentina, England head coach Thomas Tuchel has reaffirmed his commitment to the national team, vowing to remain at the helm until Euro 2028. Despite the crushing loss in Atlanta, which saw the Three Lions denied a spot in their first World Cup final since 1966, Tuchel has chosen to put the disappointment behind him and focus on the future.

item.title: Copy of Copy of Hate extra time and penalties? One man is on a mis...
item.description:
A Flawed System: The Case for Rethinking Extra Time and Penalties

It’s a scenario that has become all too familiar in the world of football: two teams locked in a stalemate, unable to find a winner in the allotted 90 minutes. The whistle blows, and the game is headed into extra time – or perhaps, if the tie remains unbroken, a grueling penalty shootout. But as the sport continues to evolve, many are beginning to question whether this traditional approach is truly fit for purpose.

item.title: American League pitchers combine for first All-Star Game shutout since 2013
item.description:
Pitching Dominance: American League Throws First All-Star Game Shutout Since 2013

Tuesday night’s All-Star Game was a resounding display of pitching prowess, as the American League held the National League to a mere three hits in a 4-0 victory. The shutout, achieved by a combination of 11 starters and 10 relievers, marked the first time the American League has achieved this feat since 2013.

The key to the AL’s success lay in the top of the first inning, where Dylan Cease took the mound and struck out the side, including Kyle Schwarber, Juan Soto, and CJ Abrams. This impressive display made Cease the seventh pitcher to accomplish the feat of striking out three batters in an All-Star Game opening inning, a distinction previously held by pitchers such as Carl Hubbell, Warren Spahn, Jim Palmer, and Pedro Martinez.

item.title: Preparing for penalties: How goalkeepers get ready...
item.description:

In a world where seconds can be the difference between triumph and heartbreak, the spotlight often falls on the stars of the game – the forwards, the midfield maestros, and the defenders who marshal the final line of defense. Yet, for all the attention lavished on these heroes, there’s another unsung protagonist whose role is just as crucial in the high-pressure world of penalty shootouts: the goalkeeper.

item.title: All the goals from France's run to semi-finals
item.description:
The Road to Glory: Unpacking France’s Semi-Final Bound World Cup Run

In a World Cup campaign marked by breathtaking skill and unwavering tenacity, France has etched its name alongside the tournament’s all-time greats. As the 2026 edition hurtles towards its climax, Les Bleus prepare to face Spain in a semi-final showdown. But what has driven this team’s success? To unravel the threads of their remarkable journey, let’s revisit every goal that has taken them to the precipice of glory.

item.title: World Cup 2026: France v Spain semi-final buildup; Rice set to start for England against Argentina – live
item.description:
Unstoppable Force Meets Immovable Object: France and Spain Gear Up for Semi-Final Showdown

As the world’s top four ranked teams prepare to face off in the World Cup semi-finals, the stage is set for a clash for the ages. item.title: Lamine Yamal enjoys birthday with a kickabout and a show before France World Cup semi-final test
item.description:
A Star in the Making: Lamine Yamal’s Unfazed Approach to World Cup Glory

Lamine Yamal’s 19th birthday was one for the books, marked by a kickabout with his mates and a show-stopping performance in the World Cup semi-final pre-match press conference. As the Spanish teenager took centre stage, his confident smile and infectious enthusiasm won over the room of journalists who had gathered to witness the spectacle. Walking in, he peeled back his tracksuit top to reveal a dazzling white gold and diamond chain that would put even the most seasoned celebrity to shame. However, in a characteristic display of humility, Yamal quickly assured the crowd that the extravagant gift was actually a self-purchase, thereby disqualifying it from being considered an official birthday present.

item.title: Deschamps predicts 'spectacular' France v Spain semi-final
item.description:
A Semi-Final Showdown for the Ages: France and Spain Gear Up for a Spectacular Clash

The stage is set for a monumental semi-final showdown in the World Cup 2026, as France and Spain prepare to face off in a highly anticipated match that promises to be nothing short of spectacular. France manager Didier Deschamps, a man with a proven track record of delivering on the biggest stages, has predicted a thrilling contest, one that will showcase the best of these two footballing powerhouses.

item.title: Manzambi picks Villa - becomes 10th player Newcastle have missed out on
item.description:
The Magpies’ Missed Opportunities: Newcastle’s Transfer Woes Continue

As the transfer market continues to unfold, Newcastle United are facing yet another setback in their pursuit of Freiburg midfielder Johan Manzambi. The 20-year-old Switzerland international has opted to join Premier League rivals Aston Villa, with Champions League football being the decisive factor in his decision. This development marks the 10th high-profile player to turn down a move to St. James’ Park since the summer of 2024.

item.title: The hardest test - Wales need reaction in South Africa

item.title: Infantino: 64-team World Cup will be 'looked at'
item.description:
A New Era for the Beautiful Game?

In a move that sent shockwaves through the football world, FIFA President Gianni Infantino has announced plans to expand the men’s World Cup to 64 teams by the next tournament. The Swiss executive’s statement has sparked both excitement and trepidation among football fans and experts alike, with many questioning the feasibility of such a drastic change.

Infantino’s comments, made at a recent press conference, suggest that the governing body is serious about giving every nation the chance to compete at the sport’s highest level. “Every nation should have the chance to dream of playing at football’s biggest event,” he said, outlining the rationale behind the proposed expansion. While the exact details of the plan remain unclear, Infantino’s words are a clear indication that FIFA is willing to take bold steps to democratize the sport.

item.title: A-List: FIFA's top-4 make WC semis for first time
item.description:
The Unprecedented Quartet

The world’s top football nations are poised to etch their names in history as Argentina, Spain, France, and England made it past the quarterfinals of the World Cup, a feat no top-four ranked teams have ever achieved in the competition’s history. Argentina, the reigning champions, have been in scintillating form, with their impressive 3-0 win against Australia setting them up for a mouth-watering clash against the Netherlands in the semis. For France, the defending runners-up, a 2-1 victory over Poland secured their spot alongside England, who edged out Senegal 3-0 in the last eight. Meanwhile, Spain, who have been struggling for consistency throughout the tournament, edged out Croatia 3-1 in a high-intensity match.

item.title: World Cup 2026: reaction to England’s quarter-final win over Norway and more – live
item.description:
Quarter-Finals Conclude: England’s Quarter-Final Win Over Norway a Mixed Bag

The quarter-finals of the World Cup 2026 have concluded, leaving only four teams in the running for the coveted title. England and Argentina will join France and Spain in the semis, a testament to their prowess on the pitch. For the first time since FIFA’s rankings began in 1992, the World Cup semi-finalists are the top four sides in the world on paper. This achievement is a significant milestone, highlighting the competitiveness and skill of the teams that have made it to this stage of the tournament.

item.title: Argentina set up England semi-final with extra-time victory over Switzerland
item.description:
Argentina’s Unyielding Spirit Propels Them Past Switzerland

In a pulsating extra-time encounter, Argentina scripted a thrilling 3-1 victory over 10-man Switzerland in Kansas City, setting up a highly anticipated World Cup semi-final showdown with England on Wednesday, 15 July. The match, marked by moments of brilliance and controversy, showcased the Argentine team’s unwavering determination and resilience.

As the match entered the high-stakes extra-time period, Argentina emerged from the shadows with a newfound sense of purpose, capitalizing on Switzerland’s numerical disadvantage to score twice and seal their semi-final berth. The Swiss, despite their valiant efforts, ultimately succumbed to the relentless pressure exerted by Argentina, whose players displayed a dogged refusal to yield. This dramatic turn of events sets the stage for a captivating encounter between Argentina and England, with the world watching in anticipation.

item.title: Rory falters as Fitzpatrick shares lead at fog-disrupted Scottish Open
item.description:
Weathering the Fog: Rory McIlroy’s Challenge at the Scottish Open

The Genesis Scottish Open at The Renaissance Club in North Berwick, Scotland, has been a test of endurance and skill for the world’s top golfers, with a thick fog rolling in to disrupt the proceedings on day three. Rory McIlroy, a favorite to win, faltered, while Matt Fitzpatrick rose to the challenge, sharing the lead with a host of other contenders.

item.title: Norway 1-2 England: World Cup quarter-final player ratings from Miami
item.description:
England’s Resilience on Display as They Edge Past Norway in Thrilling Quarter-Final Encounter

In a sweltering Miami night, England’s squad demonstrated their trademark grit and determination as they outlasted Norway 2-1 in a pulsating World Cup quarter-final encounter. The Three Lions’ victory marked a major milestone in their campaign, as they edged closer to realizing their dream of lifting the coveted trophy.

At the heart of England’s triumph was a resolute defensive display, spearheaded by the imperious Marc Guéhi, who engaged in an epic battle with his Manchester City teammate Erling Haaland. Guéhi’s tireless efforts were instrumental in limiting Norway’s attacking threat, as he marshaled the backline with a series of crucial interventions, including an eye-catching block to deny Antonio Nusa’s late shot.

item.title: 'England go home' | Norway's Viking party not ready to end
item.description:
Viking Party Unfazed as England Faces Quarter-Final Showdown

In the balmy Miami evening, a sea of Viking-clad Norwegians descended upon the city’s vibrant streets, their chants and cheers a testament to their unyielding enthusiasm. As the FIFA World Cup quarter-final showdown against England looms, Norway’s fans are poised to take centre stage, their unwavering support a defining feature of this underdog story. Gary Cotterill was on hand to capture the essence of the Norway faithful as they prepare to face one of the tournament’s favourites.

item.title: Manchester City beat Arsenal to signing of 17-year-old Jeremy Monga from Leicester

In a move that has sent shockwaves through the English football landscape, Manchester City have outmaneuvered their rivals, Arsenal, to secure the signing of 17-year-old winger Jeremy Monga from Leicester City for a reported £12.5m. This transfer is a testament to the prodigious talent of Monga, who has been touted as one of the most exciting young players in the country.

item.title: Australia v France: Nations Championship rugby union international – live
item.description:
A Crucial Test for Australia’s Rugby Ambitions

As the Wallabies take to the pitch at Suncorp Stadium in Brisbane, they face a daunting task: to break their nine-match winless streak and restore some much-needed confidence in their rugby abilities. This weekend’s match against France is more than just a game – it’s a litmus test for Australia’s standing among the world’s top nations.

The stakes are high, with the threat of home World Cup humiliation looming large in 14 months’ time. Australia’s recent form has been underwhelming, with one win from their past nine Tests, and their 31-33 loss to Ireland last weekend has left the team’s resolve to be questioned. With a new No 10 in Declan Meredith, partnered with Brumbies teammate Ryan Lonergan, the Wallabies are looking for a partnership that will bring some much-needed punch to their backline.

item.title: AFL player Nathan O’Driscoll opens up on depression and mental health struggles
item.description:

item.title: Ranking the players who could decide the Champions League semi-finals

item.title: All but back in Champions League - yet big decisions loom at Man Utd
item.description:
The Long Haul to European Glory

Manchester United’s improbable comeback in the Champions League has secured their participation in the elite competition for another season. A remarkable sequence of results has seen the Red Devils snatch a top-four finish, but in the aftermath of this improbable triumph lies a daunting reality: the true challenge is only just beginning.

The club’s hierarchy faces a defining period, marked by pivotal decisions that will shape the future of Old Trafford. The return of Champions League football, a staple of Manchester United’s identity, has alleviated the pressure on the board, but it masks the more pressing concerns. The team’s on-field struggles and the need for a sustained period of success have exposed the gaping chasm between the club’s ambition and its current capabilities.

item.title: Simons to miss rest of season and World Cup with knee injury
item.description:
A Season Shattered: Xavi Simons’ Crucial Blow to Tottenham’s Survival Hopes

Xavi Simons, the 21-year-old Dutch midfielder, has been dealt a devastating blow, his season – and potentially his World Cup dreams – hanging in the balance as he’s ruled out for the remainder of the campaign with a serious knee injury. The news sent shockwaves through the Tottenham camp, with coaches and teammates alike left reeling by the severity of the setback. As the stakes grow increasingly high for Spurs, Simons’ absence looms large, casting a dark shadow over the North London club’s desperate bid to avoid relegation.

item.title: Ospreys' Morris bouncing back after toughest year
item.description:
Rebound to Redemption

Morgan Morris, the Ospreys number eight, has been working tirelessly to overcome the toughest year of his career. The 25-year-old Welshman’s journey to redemption is set to be put to the test in the United Rugby Championship, with his coach, Mark Jones, believing that a strong finish could see him earn a first Wales call-up.

Morris’s season has been marred by injuries, setbacks, and personal struggles, which have taken a significant toll on his confidence and form. However, under the guidance of Jones, the Ospreys have shown resilience and determination, and Morris has been slowly but surely rebuilding his momentum. His coach has been instrumental in helping him navigate the challenges he has faced, and their partnership has paid dividends as Morris begins to rediscover his best self.

item.title: Xavi Simons ruled out of rest of season and World Cup with ruptured ACL
item.description:
Devastating Injury Strikes Tottenham Midfielder Xavi Simons

Xavi Simons’ season, and indeed his World Cup dreams, have been cruelly truncated after the Tottenham midfielder suffered a ruptured anterior cruciate ligament in Saturday’s 1-0 win over Wolves. The 23-year-old was stretchered off the pitch in the 63rd minute, his despairing expression a testament to the severity of the injury. Scans have since confirmed that the Netherlands international will be out for around eight months, a blow that will not only impact his club’s Premier League survival bid but also the Oranje’s chances at the World Cup finals this summer.

item.title: Xavi Simons ruled out of rest of season and World Cup with ruptured ACL
item.description:
Tragic Blow to Tottenham and Netherlands: Xavi Simons’ Season and World Cup Hopes Shattered

Xavi Simons’ world came crashing down in the 63rd minute at Molineux on Saturday, as the Tottenham midfielder’s anterior cruciate ligament gave way, ending his season and all but ruling him out of the World Cup finals for the Netherlands this summer. The devastating news has cast a pall of despair over Spurs, who were struggling to stay afloat in the Premier League, and Simons, who had been instrumental in the team’s creative play. The 23-year-old’s injury, confirmed by scans, means he will be sidelined for approximately eight months, a cruel twist of fate that has left him, and the football world, reeling.

item.title: Liverpool up to fourth but Salah injured in eventful Palace win
item.description:
A Flicker of Hope for Liverpool as Palace Win Comes at a Cost

The lights have flickered back on at Anfield, and Liverpool’s beleaguered fans can momentarily breathe a sigh of relief. A 3-1 victory over Crystal Palace has propelled the Reds up to fourth in the Premier League, but the sweet taste of success is tempered by the devastating news that star forward Mohamed Salah may have played his final game for the club. As the Egyptian international limped off the pitch with a worrying knee injury, the collective heart of the Liverpool faithful sank. The question on everyone’s lips is: what now for the Reds?

item.title: MK Dons seal promotion to League One
item.description:
Football’s Unlikely Hero: MK Dons Rise to Prominence in League One

The final whistle at Stadium MK sent shockwaves through the English football landscape as MK Dons sealed promotion to League One with a resounding 3-0 victory over Tranmere on a damp spring evening. The triumph marked a triumphant conclusion to a season that has been anything but straightforward for Paul Tisdale’s men, who have defied expectations to secure a spot in the third tier of English football. As the jubilant MK Dons faithful erupted into a frenzy of noise and colour, the reality of their achievement began to sink in – a remarkable turn of events that has catapulted this small-town club into the spotlight.
